questions.q: What kind of storage is EBS, and how does that differ from S3?
options: EBS stores data only in memory, with no persistence after the instance stops
EBS and S3 are two names for the same underlying AWS service
Block storage that behaves like a raw disk the OS formats and mounts, unlike S3's object model of whole files addressed by a key
EBS is object storage, identical in model to S3 but limited to a single Availability Zone
questions.explain: EBS is block storage — a virtual hard drive the OS can format and mount — while S3 is object storage, a completely different model built around whole files addressed by a key.

questions.q: What does gp3 deliver as its baseline performance, regardless of the volume's size?
options: gp3 has no defined performance baseline at all
Performance that scales only with volume size, with no fixed baseline
Unlimited IOPS with no throughput cap at any volume size
3,000 IOPS and 125 MB/s throughput, with the option to provision more of either
questions.explain: gp3's baseline of 3,000 IOPS and 125 MB/s is independent of volume size, and both can be provisioned higher if a workload needs it.

questions.q: What kind of workload is io2 built for, compared to gp3?
options: Only workloads that never need more than 1,000 IOPS
io2 and gp3 offer identical performance and durability in every scenario
Static website hosting, since io2 is optimized for HTTP access patterns
Workloads needing very high IOPS at low, consistent latency, such as a large transactional database, with a higher durability guarantee than gp3
questions.explain: io2 (Provisioned IOPS SSD) targets demanding, low-latency workloads and carries a 99.999% durability guarantee, higher than gp3.

questions.q: What's the real constraint on attaching an EBS volume to an EC2 instance?
options: EBS volumes can only attach to instances in a different Availability Zone from where they were created
The volume attaches to exactly one instance at a time under typical configurations, and must be in the same Availability Zone as that instance
There is no Availability Zone restriction on EBS volume attachment
A volume can attach to any number of instances simultaneously, in any Region
questions.explain: Under typical configurations an EBS volume attaches to one instance at a time, and it must sit in the same AZ as that instance since EBS doesn't span AZs.

questions.q: What happens to an EBS volume's data when its attached EC2 instance is terminated?
options: The volume's data is always destroyed immediately when the instance terminates
Termination has no effect on any attached volume under any configuration
The volume automatically converts to an S3 bucket
It depends on the Delete on Termination setting — the volume can persist independently of the instance unless that setting is on
questions.explain: Because EBS is network-attached rather than physically inside the instance, a volume's data survives independently unless Delete on Termination is enabled for it.
